title: Shared words hold different personal meanings

captions.physics: Using an understandable language of promises

meaning: You can explore familiar words thoughtfully and find a form of participation within them that preserves both people’s different wishes.
text: A shared phrase can have two personal meanings that can be connected. The Hierophant in the physical position of Vishuddha gives conversation an understandable language of promises and recognised expressions of respect. The Hermit in energy supports a search for a considered meaning of your own in the reply. Temperance in emotions brings coordination. Difference remains but stops obstructing participation. Familiar words can grow more precise through attentive discussion rather than an immediate decision about the single correct way close people ought to answer.

For example, you discuss “We need to know how to apologise”. One person wants acknowledgement of a particular sentence; the other needs to explain the original intention. **Different meanings can find room in one conversation.** Both replies can receive time: explanation need not replace apology, while apology can leave explanation possible. A familiar norm gains personal content, clarifying what participation would help finish this argument beyond outward compliance with an accepted rule.

The difficulty is discussing nuances so long for calm coordination that the needed words remain unspoken. Meaning grows clearer while the request has no direct reply. Thoughtful understanding remains good. A small, clear sentence about the particular incident helps inner agreement enter a living exchange instead of staying only a pleasant result of reasoning together.
